returnInterest.note: I for sure want to come back and travel through the entire country.

description.intro: Vietnam is a Southeast Asian country known for its diverse landscapes, vibrant cities, rich food culture, and long coastline. I found it to be an amazing and extremely affordable place to visit, with beautiful nature, welcoming people, great cities, and excellent food. Even after my trip, I felt there was still so much more of the country left to explore.
standouts: There was a huge variety of activities to experience.
I found the country very safe and easy to travel around.
Scams are fairly common, so it helps to stay alert.
Pickpocketing is common in crowded areas, but easy to deter if you keep everything in one place.
tips: Try local restaurants even if the food looks unusual.
Use common sense when choosing places to eat, to not get hit with bad food poisoning.
Go on a food tour if you are nervous about trying unfamiliar food.
Do not be afraid to negotiate prices.
Practice negotiating at markets or souvenir shops.
Remember your own financial position when negotiating very small amounts and don't over do it; 30 cents is not worth continuing to negotiate for.
You can judge prices partly based on whether a place is in a city, has seating, has a nice view, or looks luxurious; as every one of those things adds a bit to the price.
thingsToKnow: The south, especially Ho Chi Minh City/ Saigon, feels more modern.
The more north you go the cheaper it is.
Vietnam has many famous attractions such as Hang Sơn Đoòng, Ha Long Bay, and the Ha Giang Loop.
Food poisoning can happen relatively often but usually passes quickly, and is not really something to worry about.
Vietnam only has two seasons and when the rainy season starts and ends differs a lot between the north, centre, and south.
culturalNotes: People are proactive about using Google Translate to communicate.
personalNotes: Had an amazing time in Vietnam.
Regrettably didn't have enough time to visit many places.
Thought coconut coffee was the least enjoyable of the three special coffees.
Egg coffee was my absolute favorite.
Personally found Robusta coffee too bitter as plain black coffee, even though I usually only drink espresso and black coffee.
Thought drip coffee made with Moka beans is the best as the coffee made with those beans has a slight chocolate taste to it.

travelPracticalities.visaNotes: At the time I needed an E-visa which can be requested fairly easily online and lets you stay up to 90 days, with about a week or two of processing time. But now I can go Visa free for up to 45 days.
paymentNotes: Even in places that accept cards, I would recommend using cash, as there are places that will scam you through skimming your card.
VPBank and TPBank ATMs do not charge foreign transaction fees, so use them if you can find them.
Withdrawal limits are usually 5,000,000 or 20,000,000 VND and withdrawals are always given in 500,000 VND notes.
Large notes can be difficult to use with smaller vendors because they may not have enough change.
A large wallet is useful because Vietnamese notes are physically larger than euros.
transportNotes: Changing or inflated ride prices are one of the most common scams, but can be easily avoided through: discussing and agreeing on the fare in advance with taxi or other drivers when booking outside an app.

For taxi's and for other drivers that don't—want to—go through an app you can show the Grab price and usually knock a bit more off—as they don't have to pay commission. To get a good price for your ride.
You can ask drivers to wait for you if you go and do an activity outside the city where it is harder to find transport; you don't have to pay for the waiting time.
Apps like Grab or Gojek are among the easiest and most affordable ways to get around cities.
Motorcycle rides through Grab are cheaper and faster then the car options.
You can rent and drive a 50CC scooter without a driver's license.
Most driving licences are not valid in Vietnam, even if you have an international driving licence.
Hostel scooter rentals are usually safer and a lot less likely to result in scams.
Domestic flights are affordable for longer distances.
Night buses are the cheapest way to travel between cities.
VIP buses or buses with fewer than 30 seats are much more comfortable. As a third row of beds gets added from 30 seats and up.
The fewer seats a bus has, the more space and comfort you usually get.
Bus departure locations can be very confusing.
12GoAsia can be used for booking buses, but booking buses through hostels can often be cheaper and definitely less confusing.
When crossing roads; maintain a steady walking speed, avoid sudden stops, look in the direction of traffic and try to get eye contact with drivers.
Scooters and motorcycles usually drive around pedestrians.
Cars may stop, or you have to let them go in front of you.
Buses and large vehicles usually do not stop for pedestrians.
Traffic lights are usually followed, especially in the south.
languageNotes: Younger people often speak decent English.
Google Translate is commonly used for communication.
Learn some basic Vietnamese words and phrases, but be careful with pronunciation as it can completely change the meaning of words: Phở = A noodle dish, but Phò = Bitch.
packingNotes: A rain jacket that doubles as a wind breaker, would be very usefull.

seasonalNotes.season: Rainy Season (May to November (in the south))
notes: Very hot and usually sunny weather, but with a lot of quick heavy downpours; usually nothing to worry about. I personally often liked the downpours as it cooled me down a bit.

foodNotes: Local restaurants often have the best food.
Vietnam is one of the world's largest coffee exporters in the world.
Vietnamese iced coffee is very famous.
Robusta-based iced coffee is often better when ordered sweet, as the beans are quite bitter.
Good French bakeries and cheap French bread are common.
Civet coffee can be expensive at coffee farms.

regionsOverview.name: South Vietnam
notes: Represents the more modern, fast-paced and capitalistic part of Vietnam.
